notes:
Account summary
- Regulated banking prospect evaluating Redwood for internal LLM enablement platform. Primary concern is governance: export auditing, tenant/RBAC isolation, and retention controls for analytics + exports.
- Strong pull from FinOps + Security for in-console Usage Insights (cost drivers by route) and exportable reports (CSV/JSON) suitable for internal audit + cost reviews.

Key contacts (as captured in notes)
- Security lead: “We need export events in audit logs with who/when/filters; otherwise this will stall in risk.”
- FinOps lead: wants weekly cost-by-route report, plus model breakdown for chargeback.
- Platform eng: wants VPC deployment option; hosted acceptable only for non-prod experimentation.

Product fit / requirements
- Deployment: VPC (Redwood Private) preferred; Dedicated capacity also in scope for performance predictability.
- Workloads:
  - Summarization of internal case notes + call transcripts (high sensitivity).
  - Document search / RAG embeddings (medium sensitivity).
  - Support-agent copilot (sensitive, needs strict access boundaries).
- Usage Insights requirements (focus areas):
  - RBAC boundaries must be strict at org/project/environment level; no cross-project leakage in insights views or exports.
  - Exports must be audit logged (export created + download) and show user identity, time, filters, and scoping.
  - Retention controls: they want configurable retention (or at least documented retention defaults) for (a) analytics aggregates powering console views and (b) generated export artifacts.
  - Data residency: asked whether export generation/analytics run in-region for Private/VPC; if not, need an explicit statement and compensating controls.
  - Route dimension governance: they are worried teams will accidentally encode customer/account ids in route names. Asked for (1) naming guidance, (2) normalization rules, (3) guardrails/limits.

Security review progress (timeline)
- 2026-01-28: Intro + discovery. Initial interest in Usage Insights “top cost drivers by route” for internal chargeback.
- 2026-02-06: Demo of console dashboards and planned export flow. They asked: “Can we prove who exported what and when?”
- 2026-02-12: Export audit + RBAC deep dive (Gmail thread: thread-20260212-export-audit-and-rbac-review). Open items logged: audit event fields list, retention of audit logs, and how exports respect project scoping.
- 2026-02-19: Security call (Fireflies: meeting-d4e7ff02). Questions:
  - Do export events include the filter set (time range, project, environment, route/model filters)?
  - Can they forward audit logs to SIEM (at minimum via API/export)?
  - How are export files stored, how long, and who can download after creation?
  - Is there an RBAC permission distinct from “view insights” vs “export report”?
- 2026-02-23: Follow-up email from their risk team asking for: SOC2 report, audit event schema, statement on export retention + deletion, and confirmation that exports cannot cross project boundaries.

Open questions / gaps to close
- Audit logs:
  - Need definitive list of audit events for Usage Insights exports (create/download) and required fields (actor, org/project, time window, filters, row/file size, success/failure, request id).
  - They requested sample audit entries (redacted) for evidence.
- Retention:
  - They want explicit retention periods for (a) dashboard aggregates, (b) raw telemetry (if applicable), (c) export artifacts, and (d) audit logs.
  - They asked if export download links expire and whether artifacts are encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys in VPC.
- RBAC:
  - Confirm permission model: who can access route/model spend, and who can export.
  - Confirm that project scoping is enforced server-side for all insights endpoints and export jobs.
- Data residency:
  - For Private/VPC: confirm where aggregations run and where export jobs execute; if any control plane operations are multi-region, need clarity.

Internal deal notes (Redwood)
- This account is driving “export auditing + RBAC for insights” requirements harder than typical. They are a good validation design partner for regulated workflows.
- They will likely require an Enterprise security addendum + clear docs around Usage Insights export auditing.
- They explicitly said they do NOT want scheduled exports in v1, but they do want a predictable manual workflow that can be automated on their side (stable schema + bounded exports + audit logs).

Suggested next steps
1) Send security packet:
   - SOC 2 Type II, ISO statement (if available), high-level RBAC explanation for insights.
   - Usage Insights export audit events list + sample payload.
   - Retention defaults + export link expiry behavior.
2) Schedule 60-min working session with Security + FinOps:
   - Walk through export creation, expected CSV/JSON schema, and how to reconcile vs invoice totals (timing/late-arriving data).
3) If security is satisfied: propose a gated beta on a single project/environment in VPC, with strict route naming guidance and cardinality limits enabled.
